top_signal.title: How do I deal amicably with a distributor who tried to trademark my trademark?
top_signal.summary: Looking for some advice.    Tldr: My distributor tried to trademark my trademark in a different country. I paid an attorney to oppose it, and I'm asking my distributor to reimburse me. He's getting mad at the suggestion.   I have trademarked some games, and I am based in the US. I have a distributor in an overseas country, and he's been my reseller for several years.    He asked me to license my trademark to him several months ago so he could fight counterfeits, but I never gave him my permission. I actually started considering it this past week, and found that my trademark name was already pending approval in his country, and he was the one who applied for it.    It turned out he applied for the trademark about 5 months ago, and knowing that trademarks can get suddenly approved, I figured I needed to fight it immediately.    I first emailed him for clarification on his intentions and gave him 24 hours to respond.   When he didn't respond, I then paid an international attorney several hundred dollars to oppose his trademark application.    A day after that, he finally responded and said his intentions were not to steal my trademark, but get license instead. His excuse is that he didn't know what he was doing, or know the difference between owning a trademark and getting a license.    I asked him to reimburse me for my attorney's fees as he was the one who initiated the initial trademark application that I needed to fight. He's saying I should have waited for his response. (In
